rule: A candidate is not an approved dependency. Adoption requires a claim, accepted ADR when architectural, bounded task, benchmark, threat review, license review, rollback, and portability evidence.

candidates.name: Ollama
candidates.gate: Existing compatible path; verify model hashes, licenses, capability, and hardware.

candidates.name: llama.cpp
candidates.gate: Portable runtime and quantization ecosystem; benchmark per platform.

candidates.name: vLLM
candidates.gate: Throughput-oriented serving; operational and hardware requirements must be measured.

candidates.name: LocalAI
candidates.gate: OpenAI-compatible local gateway; compare with current provider path.

candidates.name: Temporal
candidates.gate: Strong durability model; compare operational cost with repository-owned executor.

candidates.name: Restate
candidates.gate: Evaluate only through the durable execution interface.

candidates.name: NATS JetStream
candidates.gate: Useful for worker profile; unnecessary for local embedded profile.

candidates.name: PostgreSQL
candidates.gate: Potential server profile; migration and local simplicity must be preserved.

candidates.name: SQLite
candidates.gate: Retain for local profile; add durability and backup discipline.

candidates.name: Qdrant
candidates.gate: Do not adopt before simple retrieval baseline and deletion tests.

candidates.name: pgvector
candidates.gate: May reduce component count in PostgreSQL profile.

candidates.name: LanceDB
candidates.gate: Evaluate portability, deletion, indexing, and operational maturity.

candidates.name: OpenSearch
candidates.gate: Heavy for local baseline; consider only for large deployments.

candidates.name: OpenTelemetry
candidates.gate: Use stable internal semantics and adapter mapping.

candidates.name: Prometheus
candidates.gate: Operational metrics only, not exact usage accounting.

candidates.name: Grafana Tempo
candidates.gate: Open-source backend candidate after telemetry contract.

candidates.name: OPA
candidates.gate: Compare with current engine before adoption.

candidates.name: SPIFFE/SPIRE
candidates.gate: Do not force into single-user local profile.

candidates.name: WASI/Wasmtime
candidates.gate: Prototype compatibility and resource controls.

candidates.name: gVisor
candidates.gate: Measure overhead and operational fit.

candidates.name: Firecracker
candidates.gate: Strong boundary with higher complexity.

candidates.name: MCP SDK
candidates.gate: All calls must pass capability broker and consent.

candidates.name: A2A SDK
candidates.gate: Adopt only after internal task and identity contracts stabilize.

candidates.name: CycloneDX
candidates.gate: Compare output needs with SPDX and existing tooling.

candidates.name: SPDX
candidates.gate: Use for license, composition, origin, and lifecycle metadata.

candidates.name: Sigstore
candidates.gate: Design offline verification and key recovery first.

candidates.name: OpenSSF Scorecard
candidates.gate: Never treat score as a guarantee.

candidates.name: restic
candidates.gate: Require restore drills and separate key custody.

candidates.name: SOPS plus age
candidates.gate: Evaluate local key custody and rotation.

candidates.name: MinIO or S3-compatible storage
candidates.gate: Verify current license, durability, and migration before adoption.
